patterns.what_worked: The three questions are answered with file:line or URL, split CONFIRMED / CONTEXT-ONLY / UNCONFIRMED. classic_era: C_SpellBook.IsSpellBookItemInRange is absent from the whole client source (ast-grep field/call/subscript forms = 0 hits; Sourcegraph plain-text on upstream classic_era = 0 content matches, which closes the ast-grep string-literal hole); Blizzard's one classic_era C_Spell.IsSpellInRange callsite is CooldownViewer.lua:713 — one argument (spell ID), result compared '== false' so nil reads as unknown, not out-of-range; the client's own generated docs give the contract (SpellDocumentation.lua:601-614: (spellIdentifier, optional targetUnit) -> bool?, nil when invalid) and show the classic client HAS the protected-function mechanism (C_RestrictedActions.CheckAllowProtectedFunctions, ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED payload) but ships NO list, comment or doc naming any protected API. The LRC audit separates by-design from broken: the legacy-global capture and the item tables are upstream design, while calling the item-range API where the client blocks it AND with a call shape invalid for the modern function is not — after the 2026-10-21 guards the vendored lib can only call CheckInteractDistance (operator's client ran it unblocked at main.lua:1791), the item/spell checker lists are never built (:596, :610, :803), and the dead call sites are :512/:809 (item) and :477/:495/:826/:842 (spell, legacy index/bookType shape, never the modern ID/name shape).
patterns.what_was_hard: ast-grep cannot see string literals inside table constructors, so every Blizzard generated API doc (the authoritative per-branch API surface) was invisible to the tool the brief suggested; I closed that by fetching the upstream raw files per branch and by adding Sourcegraph full-repo plain-text search, which found the classic_era IsSpellBookItemInRange = 0 and also revealed the classic_era doc file is INCOMPLETE (it ships C_SpellBook.GetSpellBookItemInfo, called at Blizzard_SpellSearchUtil.lua:64, but does not document it) — so absence from the doc file is weak evidence and I said so instead of treating it as proof. The web side was the other hard part: the SearxNG and Firecrawl MCP catalogs were NOT discoverable in my Code Mode catalog (search returned {"items":[]} for every query, including 'searxng' and 'firecrawl'), the operator-hosted SearxNG on localhost:8069 was unreachable from the sandbox, and DuckDuckGo/Bing/Mojeek all served bot challenges, so there was no general web-search coverage at all; I fell back to direct fetches of known URLs and to the wiki's own per-page metadata. wiki.gg was in a published offline window (502 on ~20 attempts), which is why the protected-API LIST page could not be retrieved and that gap is named instead of being papered over. Finally the orchestrator's scope correction arrived mid-lane: I re-wrote the report so no branch is generalised from classic_era, every wiki citation is labelled CONTEXT ONLY (a retail hotfix is not proof for the 1.15.x classic backport), the modern spell API appears only as an open follow-up with an exact command and never as a justification for wiring it, and the by-design/not-by-design split of the LRC is stated explicitly.
patterns.skill_gap: Three gaps remain open and are named in the report. (1) The protected state of every API except the item-range one on Era 1.15.9 is UNCONFIRMED — the operator declined the in-client probe on 2026-10-21, and only the operator's own ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED report counts as proof; wiki and forum 'protected' claims are context only. (2) Whether the legacy global IsSpellInRange exists in the 1.15.9 BINARY is UNRESOLVED: the orchestrator's shell matrix says the legacy global exists nowhere (established by grepping FrameXML source), while warcraft.wiki.gg's per-version Game Types tag for the vanilla line reads 'vanilla + 1.13.2' with no upper bound, i.e. it claims the global is still present — a binary-implemented global would not appear in FrameXML, so both can be true; FU-2's type dump settles it and decides whether the shipped LRC guards are inert on Era. (3) The complete protected-API list was NOT retrieved (wiki category page offline; the client ships no list). The desk also has no write tool, so the bench file, journal and this signal are handed over as text for the orchestrator to file.
